arm1_squares_not_order2_basis.claim: A\B = squares is NOT a basis of order 2

arm2_A_is_minimal_order1_basis.claim: A = N is a basis of order 1 and is minimal
arm2_A_is_minimal_order1_basis.why: order-1 basis means every n is itself in A, true for A = N; and for any infinite B, N\B omits every element of B, hence omits infinitely many naturals, hence is not an order-1 basis. So A = N is minimal.

arm3_counter_to_the_counterexample.B_star: the odd integers >= 3 (infinite, subset of A = N)
arm3_counter_to_the_counterexample.general_proof: n even  -> n = 0 + n, both in S;  n odd   -> n = 1 + (n-1), 1 in S and n-1 even in S. So EVERY natural is a sum of two elements of S: S is a basis of order 2, with no exceptional set at all.
arm3_counter_to_the_counterexample.verdict: A\B* IS a basis of order 2 => an infinite B with the required property EXISTS for A = N
